<meta>This page continues the philological analysis of the Ethiopic (Ge'ez) translation of the First Book of Kings, comparing it to the Greek Septuagint. The previous page listed specific omissions; this page examines the translator's stylistic inconsistencies and provides a detailed list of textual variants where the translator's Greek source manuscript differed from the standard scholarly editions of the Septuagint.</meta>

18:24 — "will answer by fire." 18:27 — "and he shall arise." 18:29 — "depart." 18:44 — "yoke your chariot." 18:45 — "here and there." 19:2 — "if you are." 19:12 — "a voice of a gentle breeze." 19:19 — "and he — twelve <note>The second instance of the number twelve in this verse</note>." 20:20 — "from horse to horseman." 21:4–5 — "a troubled spirit." 21:8 and 11 — "free men." 21:13 — "he died." 22:27 — "to eat — of affliction." 22:35 — "the battle turned." It also seems necessary to mention here that the translator sometimes swapped the third and second person of a verb or pronoun (as seen in 1:20, 27; 18:24; 21:10; 22:6, 8, 15) and that he expressed the same Greek phrases in different ways in various places. 

For example, the Greek phrase "the vain things" <note>original: τὰ μάταια</note> is translated sometimes as **unclean** <note>Ge'ez: ርኵስ, *rǝkus*</note> and other times as **vanity** <note>Ge'ez: ከንቱ, *kantu*</note> (16:2, 13, 26). The word for "ash-cakes" <note>original: ἐγκρυφίας</note> is rendered as both **baked bread** <note>Ge'ez: አኰል, *'akwal*</note> and **loaves** <note>Ge'ez: ዳናንት, *dānānt*</note> (17:12, 13). The term for "tribute" or "taxes" <note>original: φόρος</note> appears as **enemy/oppression** <note>Ge'ez: ጸር, *ṣar*</note> and **porters/burden-bearers** <note>Ge'ez: ጸዋርያት, *ṣawāryāt*</note> (4:6; 5:13, 14). The word for "temple" <note>original: ναός</note> is rendered as **sanctuary** <note>Ge'ez: መቅደስ, *maqdas*</note> or **palace/hall** <note>Ge'ez: ጽርሕ, *ṣǝrḥ*</note> (6:7, 9, 17, 33; 7:36). "The high places" <note>original: τὰ ὑψηλά, referring to ritual sites</note> are variously translated as **mountains** <note>Ge'ez: አድባር, *'adbār*</note>, **hills** <note>Ge'ez: አውግር, *'awgǝr*</note>, **gods** <note>Ge'ez: አማልክት, *'amālǝkt*</note>, or **houses of gods** <note>Ge'ez: አብያተ፡አማልክት, *'abyāta 'amālǝkt*</note> (3b:2, 3; 13:32, 33; 14:23, etc.). The common formula "the rest of the acts" <note>original: τὰ λοιπὰ τῶν λόγων</note> is sometimes **all his matters** <note>Ge'ez: ኵሉ፡ነገሩ, *kwǝllu nagaru*</note> (11:41; 15:31; 16:5, 27; 22:39, 46) and other times **the remainder of his matters** <note>Ge'ez: ተረፈ፡ነገሩ, *tarafa nagaru*</note> (16:14, 20). 

The "Book of the Chronicles" <note>original: βιβλίον λόγων τῶν ἡμερῶν</note> is translated as **the account of the days** <note>Ge'ez: ነገረ፡መዋዕል, *nagara mawā'ǝl*</note> (11:41), **the records and the year** <note>Ge'ez: ከዋያት፡ወዓመት, *kawāyāt wa-'āmat*</note> (14:29), **the records (or prophets) of the days** <note>Ge'ez: ከዋያት፡ (or ናብያት፡) መዋዕል</note> (15:7, 23; 16:5), or simply **the records** <note>Ge'ez: ከዋያት</note> (16:14, 20). However, it seems probable that this inconsistency is due more to the readers and scribes over time than to the original translator himself. 

One remarkable translation is "his young man" <note>Ge'ez: ወሬዛሁ, *warezāhu*</note> for "his younger son" <note>original: τῷ νεωτέρῳ αὐτοῦ</note> in 16:34. Also, the rendering of "elders" <note>original: πρεσβύτεροι</note> as **the elders** <note>Ge'ez: ለዛናት, *lazānāt* — a rare or possibly corrupt term</note> in 20:7–8 is alien to the translator's usual method; therefore, I suspect it was inserted by a different hand. Indeed, there are many signs that the primary version of Chapter 20 was damaged and corrupted in various ways in antiquity.

<summary>This page lists textual variations between several Ge'ez manuscripts for the end of 1 Kings Chapter 1 and the beginning of Chapter 2. It documents differences in wording regarding Solomon's rise to power and David's deathbed instructions to his son.</summary>
<keywords>Solomon, Adonijah, David, manuscript variants, critical apparatus, Kings, Ge'ez Bible, coronation, Abner, Mahanaim</keywords>

The previous page concluded with David’s final instructions; this page covers the consolidation of Solomon's throne, the fate of Adonijah and Joab (Chapter 2), and begins a section of Chapter 3 that exists in the Ethiopic and Greek traditions but is absent from the standard Hebrew Masoretic Text.</meta>

### Chapter 5

**Verse 1.** Also **Hiram** and **Hiram**. <note>original: "ኪራም"</note> The words **King of Tyre** <note>original: "ንጉሠ፡ጢሮስ"</note> before **to his son** <note>original: "ለደቁ"</note> are found in manuscript groups k and E. **They anointed him** <note>original: "ይቅብእዎ"</note>] **His God** <note>original: "የአምላኮ"</note> in Manuscript S; **When he heard that it was said, "let him reign"** [**that they anointed him king** in E] in k and E <margin>but in the margin of Manuscript E it is noted: "In another book it says: **they anointed him**, and this means they strengthened his kingdom."</margin>

### 4) Survey of the order of sections in manuscript K and the index of manuscript C.

It focuses on the translator's struggle with the Greek Septuagint source text, noting both errors and instances where the translator successfully navigated difficult passages.</meta>

19:13; 20:13; 23:24; 25. Even more striking is 22:13 **that which was found** <note>original Ge'ez: ዘተረከበ (za-tarakaba)</note> which is displaced from its proper position, or 19:27 **and I caused to be red** <note>original Ge'ez: ወአሕመርኩ (wa-ahmarku)</note> instead of **I caused to be red**. <note>original Ge'ez: አሕመርኩ (ahmarku). The translator notes an unnecessary addition of the prefix "and".</note>

Regarding the character of the version, nearly the same observations apply as those we noted above on page 4 concerning the Third Book of Kings. Since the Septuagint version itself is of inferior quality—and it is not uncommon for its phrases or even entire sentences to either lack all meaning or at least be ambiguous and obscure—it is not surprising that certain inexplicable passages also occur in the Ethiopic work, such as at the beginning of chapter 17:21, 19:25, and the end of 23:8. We are more surprised that the translator often knew how to give a tolerable meaning to awkward Greek phrasing, such as: 12:9 **man of the house**; <note>original Greek: ἀνδρὸς οἴκου</note> 14:14 **sons of mixtures**; <note>original Greek: υἱοὺς συμμίξεων (usually referring to hostages)</note> 17:11 **partners**; <note>original Greek: κοινωνούς</note> 18:16 **established**; <note>original Greek: ἐστηριγμένα</note> 18:23 **mingle yourselves**; <note>original Greek: μίχθητε (used for making a wager)</note> 19:24 **of the surrounding region**; <note>original Greek: περιοχῆς</note> 23:7 **Chettim in the grove**; <note>original Greek: χεττιῒμ τῷ ἄλσει</note> 24:14, 16 **those who shut up**. <note>original Greek: συγκλείοντες (referring to craftsmen or smiths)</note> Those foreign words, which disfigured much of the Greek interpretation <note>This refers to Hebrew words that the Greek translators did not know how to translate and instead simply transliterated into Greek letters.</note>, could not help but also disfigure the Ethiopic version: 2:14 and 10:10 **appho**; 5:19 **deblatha**; 6:8 **phelmoni**; 8:8-9 and 17:3-4 and 20:12 **maana**; 8:9 **arsis**; 10:22 **mesdaad**; 11:4, 19 **chorri** and **rasim**; 11:8, 15 **aderoth**; 11:12 **iezer**; 12:5 seq. and 22:5-6 **bedek**; 12:9 **ameibein**; 14:9 **akan**; 15:5 **apphusoth**; 19:26 **sedema**; 20:13 **nechotha**; 21:6 **theltem**; 23:4 **sademoth**; 23:5 **chomarim**, **mazouroth**; 23:7 **kadisim**, **chettim**; 23:10 **tapheth**; 23:11 **pharourim**; 23:13 **maschith**; 24:14 **theraphin**; 25:11 **charmi**, **ierebi**, 25:13 and 16 **mechonoth**; 25:14 **iamin**; 25:17 **chotar**, **sacharar**, **sabacha**. For the names of vessels, such as the **kabos** <note>original Greek: κάβος (a dry measure)</note> in 6:25 and the **basket** <note>original Greek: κάρταλλος (kartallos)</note> in 10:7, there was nothing in <term>Geez</term> <note>Ge'ez is the classical liturgical language of Ethiopia.</note> that accurately corresponded; however, words like **fine flour**; <note>original Greek: σεμίδαλις</note> 7:1 **shekel**; <note>original Greek: σίκλος</note> 7:1 et al.; **fuller**; <note>original Greek: γναφεύς (a cloth cleaner)</note> 18:17; and **sheepskin** <note>original Greek: μηλωτή</note> 2:8, 13 had already been accepted into use in the <term>Geez</term> language. But the translator seems to have thought the word **spring** <note>original Greek: κρήνη (kreine)</note> in 20:20 (compare 2 Samuel 2:13) was a proper name. He did not even attempt to translate the phrases **through the lattice** <note>original Greek: διὰ τοῦ δικτυωτοῦ</note> in 1:2 and **fairly/appropriately** <note>original Greek: ἐπιεικῶς</note> in 6:3 (compare 1 Samuel 12:22), and he substituted the word **hamol** <note>original Ge'ez: ሐሞል</note> for the word **bundle**. <note>original Greek: τολύπη</note> He interpreted incorrectly at 2:13 **he took up** <note>original Greek: ὕψωσεν (the translator mistook this for a statement about the prophet Elijah)</note>; 2:19 **the lord**; <note>original Greek: ὁ κύριος</note> 3:19 **portion** <note>original Greek: μερίς</note> (better at 3:25); 4:13 **you have been awestruck with awe**; <note>original Greek: ἐξέστησας ἔкστασιν</note> 9:8 **shut up** <note>original Greek: συνεχόμενον (see 1 Kings 21:21)</note>; 9:20 **it was in a change**; <note>original Greek: ἐν παραλλαγῇ ἐγένετο</note> 10:7 **they placed in baskets**; <note>original Greek: ἔθηκαν ἐν καρτάλλοις</note> 10:13 **the one who rules**; <note>original Greek: ἡ δυναστεύουσα</note> 10:34 **the connections which he connected**; <note>original Greek: αἱ συνάψεις ἃς συνῆψεν</note> 11:1 **she destroyed**; <note>original Greek: ἀπώλεσεν</note> 11:15 **from within** <note>original Greek: ἔσωθεν (as if it were "from the inside out")</note>; 12:1 **from the**; <note>original Greek: ἐκ τῆς</note> 12:9 and 25:8 **those guarding the threshold**, and likewise 22:4 and 23:4 **thresholds**; <note>original Greek: σταθμούς</note> 14:25 **of the Arabah**; <note>original Greek: τῆς Ἄραβα</note> 15:20 **he turned back**; <note>original Greek: ἀπέστρεψε</note> 17:13 **of the one doing**; <note>original Greek: δρῶντος</note> as well as the clauses at the end of 11:8, 14:13, 14:19, 19:21 and 22, and 19:23 (where he thought **messengers** <note>original Greek: ἀγγέλους</note> meant the angels of God). <summary>This page analyzes the linguistic quality of the Ethiopic translation of 2 Kings, noting that while the translator struggled with obscure Greek transliterations of Hebrew terms, they often provided sensible interpretations of difficult Greek phrasing. A notable recurring error is the consistent substitution of 'Persia' for Assyria and Chaldea.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the philological analysis of the Ge'ez (Ethiopic) translation of the Fourth Book of Kings (2 Kings). The previous page explored how the translator handled difficult Greek passages in the Septuagint; this page focuses on the translator's tendency to simplify the text by omitting redundant words or clarifying the meaning through explanatory additions.</meta>

<page-num>50</page-num>

He did not hesitate to omit individual words that he deemed superfluous, such as **saying** <note>original: λέγων</note> or **he said** <note>original: εἶπε</note> and others (at 1:9, 13; 11:5; 17:27, etc.); **because** <note>original: ὅτι / nam</note> at 1:4, 6; 6:16; 18:29, 31; and **participles that correspond to the Hebrew infinitive absolute** at 18:30, 33 and 19:12.

Furthermore, he omitted the following phrases:
*   1:1 **in Israel** <note>original: ἐν Ἰσραήλ</note>.
*   1:11 **another** <note>original: ἄλλον</note>.
*   1:13 **of these fifty** <note>original: τούτων τῶν πεντήκοντα</note>.
*   2:12 **he took hold of** <note>original: ἐπελάβετο</note>.
*   3:16 **trenches** <note>original: βοθύνους</note> (the second mention).
*   3:17 **of water** <note>original: ὕδατος</note>.
*   3:27 **from him** <note>original: ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ</note>.
*   4:1 **and you knew that** <note>original: καὶ σὺ ἔγνως ὅτι</note>.
*   4:9 **behold now I have known that** <note>original: ἰδοὺ δὴ ἔγνων ὅτι</note>.
*   4:10 and 11 **there** <note>original: ἐκεῖ</note>.
*   4:18 **it happened when** <note>original: ἐγένετο ἡνίκα</note>.
*   5:4 **and so** <note>original: καὶ οὕτως</note>.
*   5:11 **the leprosy** <note>original: τὸ λεπρόν</note>.
*   5:24 **from their hands** <note>original: ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν</note>.
*   6:2 **man** <note>original: ἀνήρ</note> and **one** <note>original: μίαν</note>.
*   6:12 **king** <note>original: βασιλεῦ</note>.
*   6:17 **full** <note>original: πλῆρες</note>.
*   6:32 **the messenger** <note>original: ὁ ἄγγελος</note>.
*   7:2 **officer** <note>original: τριστάτης</note>.
*   7:8 **of the part** <note>original: μέρους</note> and **and they returned from there** <note>original: καὶ ἐπέστρεψαν ἐκεῖθεν</note>.
*   7:13 *several words*;
*   7:19 **to Elisha** <note>original: τῷ Ἐλισαιέ</note>.
*   8:8 **the king** <note>original: ὁ βασιλεύς</note>.
*   8:21 **the people** <note>original: ὁ λαός</note>.
*   9:1 **of this** <note>original: τούτου</note>.
*   9:23 **his hands** <note>original: τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ</note>.
*   9:32 **toward him** <note>original: πρὸς αὐτόν</note>.
*   9:36 **the flesh** <note>original: τὰς σάρካς</note>.
*   10:9 **and he stood** <note>original: καὶ ἔστη</note>.
*   10:30 **the right thing** <note>original: τὸ εὐθές</note>.
*   14:5 **in his hand** <note>original: ἐν χειρὶ αὐτοῦ</note>.
*   16:3 **of sons** <note>original: υἱῶν</note>.
*   16:14 **thigh** <note>original: μηρόν</note>.
*   17:21 **Jeroboam** <note>original: Ἱεροβοάμ</note> (the second mention).
*   17:32 **which they did** <note>original: ἃ ἐποίησαν</note>.
*   18:17 **which is** <note>original: ἥ ἐστιν</note>.
*   19:5 **of Hezekiah** <note>original: Ἐζεκιόυ</note>.
*   19:11 **behold** <note>original: ἰδού</note>.
*   19:29 **to you** <note>original: σοι</note>.
*   20:3 **in your eyes** <note>original: ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς σου</note>.
*   20:6 **for the sake of this city** <note>original: ὑπὲρ τῆς πόλεως ταύτης</note> (the second mention).
*   21:8 **according to every command** <note>original: κατὰ πᾶσαν τὴν ἐντολήν</note>.
*   21:12 **these things** <note>original: τάδε</note>.
*   22:11 **the words** <note>original: τοὺς λόγους</note>.
*   23:17 **these words which he proclaimed** <note>original: τοὺς λόግους τούτους οὓς ἐπεκαλέሳτο</note>.
*   23:26 **of anger** <note>original: θυμοῦ</note> and **of the great** <note>original: τῆς μεγάλης</note>.
*   23:30 **of Josiah** <note>original: Ἰωσίου</note>.
*   23:35 **according to the mouth** <note>original: ἐπὶ στόματος</note> and **they gave** <note>original: ἔδωκαν</note>.
*   25:8 **of Babylon** <note>original: Βαβυλῶνος</note> (the second mention).
*   25:9 **every house** <note>original: πᾶን οἶκον</note>.
*   25:11 *several words*;
*   25:16 **of all the vessels** <note>original: πάντων τῶν σκευῶν</note>.
*   25:26 **of the face/presence** <note>original: προσώπου</note>.

Sometimes he **contracted** two words into one, such as: **he turned and went to sleep** <note>original Greek: ἐξέκλινε καὶ ἐκοιμήθη</note> became simply **he slept** <note>original Ge'ez: ቤት፡ (beta)</note> at 4:11; **he struck and killed** <note>original Greek: ἐπάታξε καὶ ἐθανάτωσε</note> became **he killed** <note>original Ge'ez: ቀተለ፡ (qatala)</note> at 15:14, 30; **he struck and killed** <note>original Greek: ἔπαισε καὶ ἐθανάτωσε</note> became **he killed** <note>original Ge'ez: ቀተለ፡ (qatala)</note> at 25:21; **ruler of the force** <note>original Greek: ἄρχων τῆς δυνάመως</note> became **commander** <note>original Ge'ez: መልአከ፡ (mal'aka)</note> at 4:13; **ordinances and judgments** <note>original Greek: δικαιώματα καὶ κρίματα</note> became **everything/all** <note>original Ge'ez: ኵሉ፡ ኵላኒ፡ (kwellu, kwellani)</note> at 17:37.

Conversely, he rendered single Greek words with two Ethiopic words, as in: 4:37 **she did obeisance** <note>original: προσεκύνησε</note>; 5:21 **he returned** <note>original: ἐπέστረψε</note>; 6:24 **he besieged** <note>original: περιεκάθισε</note>; 6:32 **shut [plural]** <note>original: ἀποκλείσαተ</note>; 7:17 **they trampled** <note>original: συνεπάτησαν</note>; 11:14 **he had stood** <note>original: εἱστήκει</note>; 17:24 **they inherited/took possession** <note>original: ἐκληρονόμησαν</note>; 17:26 **killing/putting to death** <note>original: θανατοῦντες</note>; 22:20 **I gather you** <note>original: προστίθημί σε</note>.

For the sake of clarity, he added certain words as interpretations. For example, where the years of a king's reign are counted, he always added **his reign** <note>original Ge'ez: መንግሥቱ፡ (mangestu)</note> after the word **year** <note>original Ge'ez: ዓመት፡ (amat)</note> (as seen in 3:1, 8:25, 12:1 etc., just as in Book 3, Chapter 15:9, 25, etc.). He also preceded the names of cities with the word **city** <note>original Ge'ez: ሀገረ፡ (hagara)</note> at 3:4 and 6:19; regions with **land** <note>original Ge'ez: ብሔረ፡ (behera)</note> at 4:38, 8:7, and 9; and rivers with **river** or **stream** <note>original Ge'ez: ተክለ፡ (takla) or ፈላገ፡ (falaga)</note> at 5:10, 14, 16, 4, and 7:15.

Furthermore, the following additions of this type should be noted:
*   1:4 **likewise** <note>original Ge'ez: ከማሁ፡ (kamahu)</note>.
*   1:9 **they called him** <note>original Ge'ez: ይጽውዑዎ፡ (yedaw'uwo)</note>.
*   2:2 **to Chileab** <note>original Ge'ez: ለኪሊያብ፡ (la-Kilyab)</note>.
*   2:7 **with them** <note>original Ge'ez: ምስሌሆሙ፡ (meslehomu)</note>.
*   2:8 **the Jordan** <note>original Ge'ez: ዮርዳኖስ፡ (Yordanos)</note>.
*   2:9 **both of them** <note>original Ge'ez: ከልኤሆሙ፡ (kal'ehomu)</note> and **to Elijah** <note>original Ge'ez: ለኤልያስ፡ (la-Elyas)</note>.
*   2:11 **both of them** <note>original Ge'ez: ከልኤሆሙ፡ (kal'ehomu)</note>.
*   2:23 **they began** <note>original Ge'ez: አኀዙ፡ (ahazu)</note>.
*   3:7 **with him** <note>original Ge'ez: ምስሌሁ፡ (meslehu)</note>.
*   3:24 **to Israel** <note>original Ge'ez: ለእስራኤል፡ (la-Esra'el)</note> (the second mention).
*   3:25 **men of** <note>original Ge'ez: ሰብአ፡ እሴ፡ (sab'a esse)</note>.
*   4:22 **he called him** <note>original Ge'ez: ጸውዖ፡ (daw'o)</note>.
*   4:25 **at night** <note>original Ge'ez: በለይቲ፡ (ba-layti)</note>.
*   4:31 **and he preceded him in the sunlight, Gehazi** <note>original Ge'ez: ወበደሮ፡ በጸሐይ፡ ገሃዘ፡ (wa-badaro ba-dahay Gahaza)</note>.
*   4:42 **to his servant** <note>original Ge'ez: ለቍልዔሁ፡ (la-qwal'ehu)</note>.
*   5:1 **and he honored** <note>original Ge'ez: ወያከብር፡ (wa-yakabbir)</note>.
*   5:3 **man** <note>original Ge'ez: ብእሲ፡ (be'esi)</note> and **this** <note>original Ge'ez: ዝንቱ፡ (zentu)</note>.
*   5:5 **to you** <note>original Ge'ez: ለከ፡ (laka)</note>.
*   5:10 **color** <note>original Ge'ez: ሕብረ፡ (hebra)</note> (compare Leviticus 13:2 ff.).
*   5:13 **he went** <note>original Ge'ez: ሐር፡ (hara)</note>.
*   5:14 **he went down** <note>original Ge'ez: ወረደ፡ (warada)</note>.
*   5:21 **and he returned** <note>original Ge'ez: ወተመይጠ፡ (wa-tamayta)</note>.
*   6:18 **to his tongue** <note>original Ge'ez: ለልሳኑ፡ (la-lessanu)</note> (first mention) and **Lord** <note>original Ge'ez: እግዚአ፡ (egzi'a)</note>.
*   6:26 **Israel** <note>original Ge'ez: እስራኤል፡</note>.

*   9:17 **he showed them to** <note>original Ge'ez: አርአዮሙ፡ ለ፡ (ar'ayomu la)</note>.

*   10:20 **to them** <note>original Ge'ez: ሎሙ፡ (lomu)</note>.
*   11:10 **Jehoiada** <note>original Ge'ez: ዮዳሔ፡ (Yodahe)</note> instead of **the priest** <note>original Greek: ὁ ἱερεύς</note>.
*   12:6 **the people saw... that...** <note>original Ge'ez: ሰባ ርእየ... ከመ (saba re'ya... kama)</note>.
*   14:9 **thistle/thorn** <note>original Ge'ez: ፅዕ፡ (de')</note> (twice).
*   14:11 **and he was found with** <note>original Ge'ez: ወተረክበ፡ ምስሌ፡ (wa-tarakba mesle)</note>.
*   14:19 **from there** <note>original Ge'ez: እምህየ፡ (em-heyya)</note>.

*   14:21 **Amon** <note>original Ge'ez: አሚነ፡ (Amine)</note>.
*   15:4 **there** <note>original Ge'ez: ህየ፡ (heyya)</note>.

*   18:21 **they break it** <note>original Ge'ez: ይሰብርዎ፡ (yesabrewo)</note> and **remission/forgiveness** <note>original Ge'ez: ስርየተ፡ (seryata)</note>.

*   20:2 **he says** <note>original Ge'ez: ይብል፡ (yebel)</note> instead of **saying** <note>original Greek: λέγων</note>.

He translated individual phrases periphrastically rather than word-for-word...

<summary>This page analyzes the translation style of the Ge'ez version of 2 Kings, noting where the translator omitted superfluous Greek words or added explanatory terms (like "city" or "land") to make the text more readable and culturally accessible.</summary>
<keywords>Ge'ez, translation technique, Biblical philology, Septuagint, omissions, interpretive additions, 2 Kings, linguistics</keywords>

--- Page 1069 ---
<meta>This page continues the philological analysis of the Ge'ez (Ethiopic) translation of the Second Book of Kings. While the previous page listed specific omissions made by the translator to streamline the text, this page examines instances where the translator prioritized the overall meaning (the "sense") over a word-for-word literal translation of the Greek Septuagint. It also begins a comparison between the Ge'ez version and the standard Greek manuscript traditions to identify which specific Greek source the translator might have been using.</meta>

<page-num>51</page-num>

As seen in 3:21, 25; 4:8, 24; 5:4 (at the beginning); 5:12; 6:22; 7:4 (at the beginning); 10:24, 29; 15:20; 16:13; 17:10; 18:10; 19:3; 23:26, 35; 25:7, 29, 30—and especially in 12:11–17; 13:21; 18:20—the translator expressed the sense of the Greek words rather than the words themselves in many places:

*   1:7 **judgment** <note>original Greek: κρίσις (krisis)</note>.
*   1:13 **he begged** <note>original Greek: ἐδεήθη (edeēthē)</note>.
*   4:6, 16 **you will go down** <note>original Greek: καταβήσῃ (katabēsē)</note>.
*   2:12 **chariot and horseman** <note>original Greek: ἅρμα καὶ ἱпπεύς (harma kai hippeus); translated more accurately in 13:14</note>.
*   3:10 and 13 **he called those passing by** <note>original Greek: κέκληκε παρερχομένους (keklēke parerchomenous)</note>.
*   4:1 **of sons** <note>original Greek: υἱῶν (huiōn)</note>.
*   4:35 **he returned** <note>original Greek: ἐπέστρεψε (epestrepse)</note>.
*   4:38 **set [the pot] on** <note>original Greek: ἐπίστησον (epistēson)</note>.
*   4:40 **he poured in** <note>original Greek: ἐνέχεε (enechee); translated more accurately in verse 41</note>.
*   5:10 and 12 **to be cleansed** <note>original Greek: καθαρίζεσθαι (katharizesthai)</note>.
*   5:23 **they took up** <note>original Greek: ἦραν (ēran)</note>.
*   6:2 **let us take** <note>original Greek: λάβωμεν (labōmen)</note>.
*   6:7 **they lifted for themselves** and **he reached out** <note>original Greek: ὕψωσαν σεαυτῷ (hupsōsan seautō) and ἐξέτεινε (exeteine)</note>.
*   6:11 **he betrays me** <note>original Greek: προδίδωσί με (prodidōsi me)</note>.
*   6:24 **he went up** <note>original Greek: ἀνέβη (anebē)</note>.
*   6:31 **it shall stand** <note>original Greek: στήσεται (stēsetai)</note>.
*   8:4 **he spoke** <note>original Greek: ἐλάλησε (elalēse)</note>.
*   8:9 **he stood before** <note>original Greek: ἔστη ἐνώпιον (estē enōpion)</note>.
*   8:11 **he stood until he was ashamed** <note>original Greek: ἔστηκεν ἕως αἰσχύνης (estēken heōs aischunēs)</note>.
*   9:15 **it is your soul** <note>original Greek: ἔστι ψυχὴ ὑμῶν (esti psychē hymōn)</note>.
*   9:17–19 **horseman** <note>original Greek: ἐπιβάτης (epibatēs)</note>.
*   9:21 **yoke [the chariot]**, **they yoked** <note>original Greek: ζεῦξον, ἔζευξαν (zeuxon, ezeuxan)</note>.
*   9:24 and likewise 13:16 **he filled his hand with the bow** <note>original Greek: ἔпλησε τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ τόξῳ (eplēse tēn cheira autou en tō toxō)</note>.
*   9:27 **he died** <note>original Greek: ἀπέθανε (apethane)</note>.
*   11:16 **they laid hands** <note>original Greek: ἐπέθηκαν χεῖρας (epethēkan cheiras)</note>.
*   12:5 following: **to seize** <note>original Greek: κρατεῖν (kratein)</note> and 12:12 **to hold fast** <note>original Greek: κατέχειν (katechein)</note>.
*   12:8 **from the people** <note>original Greek: παρὰ τοῦ λαοῦ (para tou laou)</note>.
*   13:7, 14 **horsemen** <note>original Greek: ἱпπεῖς (hippeis)</note>.
*   14:6 **above** <note>original Greek: ὑπέρ (hyper)</note>.
*   14:7 **he seized the rock** <note>original Greek: συνέλαβε τὴν πέτραν (sunelabe tēn petran)</note>.
*   15:5 **in (a house)** <note>original Greek: ἐν (οἴκῳ) (en oikō)</note>.
*   15:19 **his hand to be with him** <note>original Greek: εἶναι τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ μετ' αὐτοῦ (einai tēn cheira autou met' autou)</note>.
*   16:5 **to make war** <note>original Greek: πολεμεῖν (polemein)</note>.
*   17:4 **he found wickedness in him** <note>original Greek: εὗρεν ἀδικίαν ἐν αὐτῷ (heuren adikian en autō)</note>.
*   18:30 **it may be delivered into [his] hand** <note>original Greek: παραδοθῇ ἐν χερί (paradothē en cheri)</note>.
*   20:7 **to place upon** <note>original Greek: ἐπιτιθέναι (epitithenai)</note>.
*   20:15 **they saw** <note>original Greek: εἶδον (eidon)</note>.
*   21:14 **inheritance** <note>original Greek: κληρονομία (klēronomia)</note>.
*   22:13 **according to all that is written against us** <note>original Greek: κατὰ пάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα καθ' ἡμῶν (kata panta ta gegrammena kath' hēmōn)</note>.
*   23:29 **to see** <note>original Greek: ἰδεῖν (idein)</note>.
*   24:4 **innocent blood** <note>original Greek: τὸ αἷμα ἀθῶον (to haima athōon)</note>.
*   24:11 **servants** <note>original Greek: παῖδες (paides)</note>.
*   24:14 **poor of the land** <note>original Greek: πτωχοὶ τῆς γῆς (ptōchoi tēs gēs)</note>.
*   25:1 **he built a wall around [it]** <note>original Greek: ᾠκοδόμησε περίτειχος κύκλῳ (ōkodomēse periteichos kyklō)</note>.
*   25:19 **those seeing the face** <note>original Greek: τῶν δρώντων τὸ пρόσωπον (tōn drōntōn to prosōpon)</note>.
*   25:27 **he lifted the head** <note>original Greek: ὕψωσε τὴν κεφαλήν (hupsōse tēn kephalēn)</note>.

*Changes in the person of verbs* are found in 3:13; 12:7; 22:17; likewise *changes in the grammatical number of verbs* in 18:7, 22, 25; 19:7, 29; 23:6.

To this point, it also seems relevant to mention that he expressed the same Greek words differently in various places, such as:
*   **Year** <note>original Greek: ἔτος (etos)</note> sometimes as ዓመት፡ <note>Ge'ez: ʿamat</note>, sometimes as ክረምት፡ <note>Ge'ez: kremt, literally 'rainy season' or 'winter'</note>.
*   **Officer/Captain** <note>original Greek: τριστάτης (tristatēs)</note> in 7:2, 7:17, 19; 9:25; 10:25; 15:25.
*   **Conspired** <note>original Greek: συνεστράφη (sunestraphē)</note> in 9:14; 10:9; 14:19 and others.
*   **Wall-builders/Siege-workers** <note>original Greek: τειχισταί (teichistai)</note> in 12:12 and 22:6.
*   **To bend down** <note>original Greek: συγκύпτειν (synkyptein)</note> in 16:17; 18:16.
*   **Mouth to mouth** <note>original Greek: στόμα εἰς στόμα (stoma eis stoma)</note> in 10:21; 21:16.
*   **To rebel/break faith** <note>original Greek: ἀθετεῖν (athetein)</note> (just as in the Third Book <note>1 Kings</note>) sometimes as ወለወ፡ <note>Ge'ez: walawa, to turn away or change</note> in 3:22; 18:20, and sometimes as አዕረፈ፡ <note>Ge'ez: aʿrafa, to rest or cease—possibly a misreading or specific interpretation</note> in 1:1; 18:7; 24:20 (compare with **hemmed in** <note>original Greek: συνεχόμενον (synechomenon)</note> in 9:8 with 1 Kings 21:21, and **frames/borders** <note>original Greek: συγκλείσματα (synkleismata)</note> in 16:17 with 1 Kings 7:15 following).

However, in other phrases found throughout the book, there is greater consistency than in the third book (see above, page 6):
*   **The rest of the acts** <note>original Greek: τὰ λοιпὰ τῶν λόγων (ta loipa tōn logōn)</note> is everywhere translated as ኵሉ፡ ነገር፡ <note>Ge'ez: kʷellu nagar, 'all things/matters'</note> (1:18; 8:23; 12:19 and others).
*   **Book of the chronicles** <note>original Greek: βιβλίον λόγων τῶν ἡμερῶν (biblion logōn tōn hēmerōn)</note> is everywhere (except 12:19 and 13:8, 12) translated as መጽሐፈ፡ ነገሥትሙ፡ <note>Ge'ez: mas'hafa nagaśtmu, 'the book of their kings'</note>.
*   **High places** <note>original Greek: ὑψηλά (hupsēla)</note> translated as አብያተ፡ አማልክት፡ <note>Ge'ez: abyāta amālekt, 'houses of gods'</note>.
*   **Sacred grove/Asherah** <note>original Greek: ἄλσος (alsos)</note> translated as ምስራቆም፡ <note>Ge'ez: mesrāqomu, 'their place of rising/east'</note> or ምስራቅ፡ <note>Ge'ez: mesrāq, 'east'</note> (and only in 23:6 as ምስለ፡ አማልክት፡ <note>Ge'ez: mesla amālekt, 'with the gods'</note>).
*   The expression **the ears shall tingle** <note>original Greek: ἠχήσει τὰ ὦτα (ēchēsei ta ōta)</note> in 21:12 is translated the same way as in 1 Samuel 3:11.
*   **Long live the king** <note>original Greek: ζήτω ὁ βασιλεύς (zētō ho basileus)</note> in 11:12 is translated the same way as in 1 Kings 1:25, 34, 39.

---

->2) Overview of readings that the translator had in his Greek manuscript, which differ from<-
->the Holmesian Septuagint text.<-

*   1:2 **my** <note>original Greek: μου (mou)</note> added after **sickness** <note>original Greek: ἀῤῥωστίας (arrōstias)</note>. **For his sake** <note>original Greek: αὐτοῦ χάριν (autou charin)</note> instead of **through him** <note>original Greek: δι' αὐτοῦ (di' autou)</note>.
*   1:3 **of Ahaziah** <note>original Greek: 'Οχοζίου (Ochoziou)</note> added.

Verse 8. **See Verse 6.** Manuscripts k and E read **Nista** and **Nista**. <note>This likely refers to a variation in the name of the Queen Mother, Nehushta.</note>

Verse 9. **Before:** manuscript E adds **his eyes**.

Verse 10. **He went up:** manuscript k reads **his servants went up**; manuscript E has this reading in the line. **And it was besieged:** manuscripts B and C read **and it was surrounded and it was shut**; manuscripts D and R read **and it was shut**; manuscript E reads **and it was surrounded**. **And they were taken captive:** manuscript E reads **in captivity**.

Verse 11. **They fought — he commanded:** manuscript E reads **and his servants fought**.

Verse 12. **With:** manuscript k adds **his mother and**; manuscript E reads **he and his mother and**. **And he gathered:** omitted in manuscripts k and E. **His kingdom:** manuscript E adds **of Nebuchadnezzar**.

Verse 13. **And he brought out:** manuscript E adds **from there**. **As the Lord said:** omitted in manuscripts S and R.

Verse 14. **All:** manuscripts k and E read **and all**; manuscript A reads **all**. **9:** <note>The number 9,000</note> manuscript E reads **ten thousand**. **Their craftsmanship:** <note>original: "ኪነቶሙ" (kinatomu), referring to the artisans and smiths</note> manuscripts B, R, and E (likewise in Verse 16). **Bada:** <note>original: "በደ"</note> manuscripts C, R, and E.

Verse 15. **To Jehoiachin:** manuscripts B, C, and E add **into**. **Their exile:** manuscript k reads **and their exile**. **All of them:** manuscript k reads **for all of them**; manuscripts B and C add **into**; manuscript E adds **from Jerusalem**.

Verse 16. **All:** manuscript k reads **and for all**; manuscript E reads **and all**. **Strong ones:** manuscript k.

Verse 17. **To Nathan:** <note>original: "ለናታን" (la-Natan), a variant of Mattaniah, the birth name of King Zedekiah</note> manuscripts A and k.

Verse 18. **Jeremiah:** manuscript k adds **who is from Libnah**; manuscript E adds **who is from Lomna**.

Verse 20. **He brought them out:** manuscript E reads **he cast them out**.

### Chapter 25.

Verse 1. **Month:** manuscript k adds **and on the tenth of that month**; manuscript E adds **and on the tenth of the new moon**. **With:** manuscript E reads **he and all**. **Upon:** manuscript k reads **toward**.

Verse 2. **On:** omitted in manuscript k. **9th [day] of the new moon:** manuscript E reads **nine of the new moon**; manuscript k reads **nine for the new moon**. **Month:** manuscript k adds **fourth**.

Verse 3. **Great:** manuscripts S, k, and E. **Famine:** manuscript E adds **in the city**. **For the people:** manuscript E.

Verse 4. **And it was breached:** manuscript E reads **and it was split**. **Middle:** manuscript E reads **middle of the walls**. **They governed it:** <note>original: "መገብዋ"</note> manuscripts R and E read **while they were piercing it**. **Persia:** <note>The Ge'ez scribe likely confused the names of the conquering empires</note> manuscript k reads **Chaldeans**; manuscript E reads **Chaldean**; likewise in the following commentaries.

Verse 5. **And they pursued them:** manuscripts A, k, and E. **And they seized him:** manuscript k reads **and they found him**. **And they fled:** manuscript E reads **and they were scattered**.

Verse 6. **In Riblah:** <note>original: "ይበሉታ" (Yebeluta)</note> manuscript k reads **in Deblata of Jerusalem** (as written). **And he spoke:** manuscripts k and E add **judgment**.

Verse 7. **And he blinded him:** manuscript k (except D) and manuscript A; manuscript k (except D) and manuscript E add **his eyes**. **And he bound him:** manuscript E adds **with bronze**.

Verse 8. **Seventh:** manuscripts k and E read **fifth**. **He came (2nd instance):** manuscript k adds **to**.

Verse 9. **And he burned (2nd instance):** manuscripts R and E read **and he burned all the great houses with fire**. **Chief — for the King:** omitted in manuscript k (except R).

Verse 10. **Walls:** manuscript E.

Verse 11. **Who remained:** manuscript E adds **many**. **Into the [Chaldeans] — [Jeremiah]:** omitted in manuscripts k and E.

Verse 12. **Nation:** manuscript k reads **land**. **And for the plowing:** manuscript E reads **and for the wine-press**. **For the counting — and for the plowing:** manuscript k reads **for the vineyard and for the harvest**.

Verse 13. **They broke it:** manuscripts k and E read **they broke**. — See Verse 4. — And they brought in: manuscripts k and A.

Verse 14. **And the pots also:** manuscripts k and E (likewise the following names in the Accusative case). **And the bowls also:** manuscripts B, C, and R add **and the plates also**. **All:** manuscripts B and R read **and all**.

Verse 15. **Gold and silver:** <note>manuscript variation in phrasing</note> **that which was of gold, gold, and that which was of silver.**

->Corrections to be made in the text of the fourth book<-

->Chapter 20, verse 6, where you should read **and I will save you** <note>original: "ወአድኅነከ" (wa’adhěnaka)</note> instead of **and I will save you** <note>original: "ወአድኀነከ" (wa’adhanaka)</note><-
<note>This correction highlights a subtle spelling difference. In the Ge'ez language, there are multiple characters for the 'h' sound (in this case ኀ and ኅ). While they sound similar, scholars insisted on using the linguistically "correct" version to maintain the purity of the classical text.</note>
